name: Netherlands
genZNote: Roughly a quarter of the Netherlands sits below sea level — the country has spent centuries literally building itself out of the sea with dikes and windmills, making 'God made the world, but the Dutch made the Netherlands' a genuinely earned saying.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: A small, low-lying country in Northwestern Europe on the North Sea, bordered by Germany and Belgium, with roughly a quarter of its land area below sea level.
Famous for its extensive network of dikes, polders (reclaimed land), and windmills historically used for water management and drainage.
One of the most densely populated countries in the world, with flat terrain well-suited to cycling infrastructure and agriculture.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Dutch is the official language; the country has a long tradition of religious and social tolerance and progressive social policies.
Home to world-renowned artistic heritage, including Golden Age painters Rembrandt and Vermeer, and modern masters like Van Gogh.
Cycling is deeply embedded in daily culture, supported by extensive dedicated cycling infrastructure nationwide.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A parliamentary constitutional monarchy; the King is head of state while an elected Prime Minister leads the government, with a bicameral States-General as parliament.
Historically a major seafaring and colonial power through the Dutch East India Company (VOC), one of the first major multinational trading corporations.
Known for a strong consensus-based political culture ('polder model') that emphasises negotiation and compromise across social groups.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A world leader in water management engineering, hydraulic infrastructure, and flood-control technology, expertise it exports globally.

Home to advanced semiconductor equipment manufacturing (ASML, a critical global supplier of chip-making machines) and strong agricultural technology (a top global agri-exporter despite its small size).
Strong biomedical and pharmaceutical research base, alongside globally respected universities and research institutions.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A founding member of the European Union and NATO, and host to major international institutions including the International Court of Justice at The Hague.
Historically influential as a major global trading and colonial power, with lasting cultural and economic links to former colonies including Indonesia and Suriname.
An active advocate for international law and multilateralism, reflected in The Hague's role as a global centre for international justice.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and the Netherlands share a 'Strategic Partnership', with the Netherlands being one of India's largest sources of foreign direct investment via Dutch holding companies.
Strong cooperation in water management technology, agriculture, and horticulture, areas of direct relevance to Indian agricultural modernisation.
Rotterdam serves as a major European gateway port for Indian trade with Europe.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A highly developed, trade-oriented economy; the Port of Rotterdam is one of the largest and busiest ports in Europe.
A surprisingly major global agricultural exporter (second only to the US in agricultural export value) despite its small size, driven by advanced greenhouse and farming technology.
Home to major multinational companies (Shell, Philips, ASML, Unilever) and a significant global financial and logistics hub.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Its extensive water management engineering and land reclaimed from the sea (polders).
Tulips, windmills, and Golden Age art (Rembrandt, Vermeer).
Being the world's second-largest agricultural exporter by value despite its small size.
Hosting the International Court of Justice at The Hague.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Netherlands is a low-lying Northwestern European parliamentary constitutional monarchy, a founding EU/NATO member famous for water management engineering and global trade.
keyFacts: Capital: Amsterdam (seat of government: The Hague). Currency: Euro.
Parliamentary constitutional monarchy; bicameral States-General parliament.
About a quarter of its land lies below sea level, managed via dikes and polders.
World's second-largest agricultural exporter by value despite its small size.
commonConfusion: Amsterdam is the Netherlands' constitutional capital, but the seat of government, parliament, and most embassies is actually The Hague.

highYieldFacts: Netherlands: parliamentary constitutional monarchy; capital Amsterdam, government seat The Hague.
World's 2nd-largest agricultural exporter by value; global water-management engineering leader.
India-Netherlands: Strategic Partnership; major FDI source for India via Dutch holding companies; Rotterdam is a key EU trade gateway.
commonTraps: Confusing Amsterdam (constitutional capital) with The Hague (actual seat of government and international courts).
Assuming the Netherlands' small size limits its agricultural export power — it ranks second globally by value.
mustRemember: Netherlands: constitutional monarchy, water-engineering leader, top agri-exporter, major India FDI and trade gateway via Rotterdam.
